definition: A filtered-popping recursive transition network (FPRTN), or simply filtered-popping network (FPN), is a recursive transition network (RTN) extended with a map of states to keys where returning from a subroutine jump requires the acceptor and return states to be mapped to the same key.
details: RTNs are finite-state machines that can be seen as finite-state automata extended with a stack of return states; as well as consuming transitions and ε {\displaystyle \varepsilon } -transitions, RTNs may define call transitions. These transitions perform a subroutine jump by pushing the transition's target state onto the stack and bringing the machine to the called state. Each time an acceptor state is reached, the return state at the top of the stack is popped out, provided that the stack is not empty, and the machine is brought to this state. Throughout this article we refer to filtered-popping recursive transition networks as FPNs, though this acronym is ambiguous (e.g.: fuzzy Petri nets). Filtered-popping networks and FPRTNs are unambiguous alternatives.

explainer.lead: A filtered-popping recursive transition network is a finite-state machine that can jump into subroutines and keep a stack of places to return to. It adds keys to states so that a return is allowed only when the acceptor state and the saved return state have the same key.

tiers.eli5: Imagine reading a choose-your-own-adventure book and leaving bookmarks whenever you jump to another section. Each bookmark and each ending has a color, and you may go back only when the ending and the top bookmark have the same color. The bookmarks keep track of where to continue, while the colors stop you from returning to the wrong place.
tiers.practitioner: Implement it as an RTN interpreter with a return-state stack and an additional key lookup when popping. Consuming, ε-, and call transitions behave as usual, but an acceptor state can complete a return only when its key matches the key of the state at the top of the stack. A pitfall is checking only that the stack is nonempty, which would reproduce ordinary RTN popping rather than filtered popping.
tiers.paperLevel: An FPRTN is an RTN extended with a map k: Q → K from states to keys. A call transition pushes its target return state r onto the stack and enters the called state; at an acceptor state a, the machine may pop r and resume there only if the stack is nonempty and k(a) = k(r). The abbreviation FPN is ambiguous because it can also mean fuzzy Petri net.

explainer.example: Suppose a call saves return state r, with key A, and the machine reaches acceptor state a. If a also has key A, the machine pops r and continues from r; if a has key B, that return is not allowed.

components.name: States and transitions
components.detail: The finite-state control supports consuming transitions and ε-transitions, as well as calls into subroutines.

components.name: Call transitions
components.detail: A call pushes its target state as a return state and moves the machine to the called state.

components.name: Return-state stack
components.detail: The stack records pending return locations, with the most recently saved location on top.

components.name: Acceptor states
components.detail: Reaching an acceptor state can trigger a return by popping the stack when it is nonempty and the key test passes.

components.name: State-to-key map
components.detail: This map assigns a key to each state and supplies the two keys compared during a return.

flow: The machine follows consuming or ε-transitions during ordinary finite-state operation.
On a call transition, it pushes the transition's target state onto the return-state stack.
It then jumps to the called state and continues running the subroutine.
When an acceptor state is reached, the machine examines the return state at the top of a nonempty stack.
It pops that state and resumes there only if the acceptor and return states have the same key.
explainer.lineage: It extends a recursive transition network, which itself extends a finite-state automaton with a stack of return states. FPRTN and filtered-popping network are unambiguous names, while FPN can also refer to fuzzy Petri nets.
explainer.whyItMatters: The key comparison filters which pending return an acceptor state may complete. This makes subroutine returns more selective than ordinary RTN popping while leaving the other transition behavior intact.

nodes.label: Normal transition
nodes.note: Consumes input or takes an ε-transition.

nodes.label: Call transition
nodes.note: Saves a return state and enters a subroutine.

nodes.label: Acceptor state
nodes.note: Offers to return from the subroutine.

nodes.label: Matching keys
nodes.note: Allows the pop only when both state keys agree.

diagram.caption: Calls save return states on a stack; acceptor states can pop them only after the state-key check succeeds.
